input: Draft a volunteer agreement for my nonprofit board

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Board volunteer agreements can range from a simple one-page commitment letter to a comprehensive legal document covering confidentiality, conflicts of interest, liability, and term limits — knowing what to include or exclude shapes the entire structure.

The agreement may need to be tailored depending on whether it covers all board members equally, distinguishes officer roles (e.g., Chair, Treasurer), or applies to advisory board members vs. governing board members.
The nonprofit's mission, size, and sector (e.g., arts, healthcare, education) affect what responsibilities and commitments are realistic and relevant to include.

Legal requirements for volunteer agreements vary by jurisdiction, and whether the user needs the document to be attorney-reviewed or self-sufficient affects how formal and legally precise the language must be.
Tone can range from warm and values-driven to formal and contractual — this affects how board members perceive and respond to signing the document.
Knowing whether the primary goal is legal protection, clear expectation-setting, accountability, or onboarding culture determines which sections get the most emphasis.
The intended format (Word doc, PDF, fillable form) and whether it will be signed digitally or in person affects how the document should be structured and delivered.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a volunteer agreement for nonprofit board
gold.taskDescription: Create a volunteer agreement document for the user's nonprofit organization that outlines the terms, responsibilities, and expectations for board members.

questions.title: What specific sections must the agreement cover?
questions.description: Determine which clauses to include — e.g., time commitment, confidentiality, conflict of interest, liability waiver, term length, or a simple roles-and-responsibilities overview.

questions.title: Does this cover all board members or specific roles?
questions.description: Clarify whether the agreement applies uniformly to all board members or needs to distinguish between officer roles (Chair, Treasurer, Secretary) or governing vs. advisory board members.

questions.title: What is your nonprofit's mission or sector?
questions.description: Understand the organization's focus area (e.g., health, education, arts, social services) and size so the responsibilities and commitments reflected in the agreement are realistic and relevant.

questions.title: Which country or state governs this agreement legally?
questions.description: Identify the jurisdiction to ensure the document's language aligns with applicable nonprofit and volunteer law, and whether it needs to meet any regulatory requirements.

questions.title: Should the tone be formal/legal or warm and values-driven?
questions.description: Determine whether the document should read like a binding contract with precise legal language or a collaborative commitment letter that reflects the organization's culture.

questions.title: What is the main purpose — accountability, legal protection, or onboarding?
questions.description: Identify the primary goal of the document so the most critical sections receive the right emphasis — e.g., enforceable obligations, liability coverage, or welcoming new board members.

questions.title: What format and signing method will you use?
questions.description: Confirm the desired output format (Word, PDF, fillable form) and whether signatures will be collected digitally (e-signature platform) or on paper, to structure the document accordingly.
